page: Google Cloud Platform g1-small is a budget-tier virtual machine instance featuring 1 vCPU allocated from a shared physical Intel Xeon core running at 2.3 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.7 GB of memory per core, and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. The processor features a 45 MB L3 cache and supports hardware flags such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES cryptography, and FMA.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tier of cloud resources. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both yield a score of 1076.89, placing the instance in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is limited, with large-block read speeds at 10.49 GB/sec and write speeds at 8.91 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores are 1263.03 and 792.89 respectively, reflecting its shared-core architecture. Static web serving throughput is measured at 0.54 GB/sec, and small-model 135M LLM text generation operates at 20.22 tokens/sec.

Due to its shared-core configuration and low resource allocation, the g1-small offers high qualitative cost efficiency for lightweight, non-continuous workloads. It is designed for low-demand applications that do not require sustained CPU performance. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, small-scale development or testing environments, lightweight background tasks, and simple utility scripts that can tolerate shared-core resource contention.
